agent: the game options wave, reader B (2026-11-04)
question: The in-game settings window's Video tab (menu_settings_VIDEO) whole: resolution, refresh rate and multisampling - where each list comes from, its order, a value's text, the buttons' ends and greying; gamma_slider, counter_slider and counter_scale_slider - range, step, text, the setting each holds; the five checkboxes; for each control at once or on Apply, and whether it needs a restart.

structs.name: DisplayMode
structs.comment: One screen size the adapter offers, an element of the settings' display mode list (GameSettings +0x14 .. +0x18): the width and height and the refresh rates enumerated for that size, in the order the driver enumerated them. Made by GraphicsSettings_AddDisplayMode; no RTTI. The dword at +0x10 is the refresh vector's capacity end; +0x14 was not read. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
structs.evidence: The 0x18 stride: every walk of the list divides by 24 (imul 0x2AAAAAAB; sar 2 at 0x6F735D, 0x6F93CA, 0xAA6D55) and steps `add ecx, 0x18` (0x6F7390, 0x6F93FA, 0xAA6D7D). The layout: GraphicsSettings_AddDisplayMode builds the new element on its stack as [ebp-0x28] width, [ebp-0x24] height, [ebp-0x20]/[ebp-0x1C]/[ebp-0x18] the int vector (0xAA6D86-0xAA6DBA). Shown wrong by any reader of +0x14 that uses it as something other than padding.

structs.name: MultisampleLevel
structs.comment: One entry of g_MultisampleLevels (15 of them, samples 2 to 16): the sample count, whether the adapter supports it, and its highest quality level. GraphicsSettings_DetectDevice fills the last two with IDirect3D9::CheckDeviceMultiSampleType at startup; the settings window's multisampling buttons step through the entries whose `supported` is set. No RTTI; the name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
structs.evidence: The static image holds {2,0,0} .. {16,0,0} at 12-byte steps from VA 0x170A100 to 0x170A1B4 (read with image.read). The detection writes `mov byte [eax], 1` and `mov [eax+4], quality-1` with eax walking from 0x170A104 by 12 (0xAA4397, 0xAA43F6-0xAA4409, 0xAA4659). Shown wrong by a reader that treats +8 as anything but the quality count.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::InitVideoTab
addresses.comment: **Finds the Video tab's sliders and checkboxes and hangs their observers on them**, from the constructor (0x6F6831, after the Game tab's 0x6F68F0). Each is looked up in `menu_settings_VIDEO` (the gui's slot 27 for the window, then the window's slot 18 for a checkbox or slot 19 for a scrollbar) and kept, and its observer registered through the element's +0x48 interface slot 1: trees_checkbox +0x328 (observer +0x260, OnTreesCheckbox), gamma_slider +0x338 (+0x280, OnGammaSlider), counter_slider +0x33C (+0x298, OnCounterSlider), counter_scale_slider +0x340 (+0x2B0, OnCounterScaleSlider), water_checkbox +0x32C (+0x2C8, OnWaterCheckbox), hierarchy_checkbox +0x330 (+0x2E8, OnHierarchyCheckbox), unit_name_checkbox +0x334 (+0x308, OnUnitNameCheckbox). The two counter sliders are null-checked before their observer goes on; the four checkboxes and the gamma slider are not, so a mod's settings.gui without one of those five likely crashes here (inferred: what the window's lookup answers for a missing name was not read). **`counters_checkbox` gets no observer** - StoreChoices reads its state directly. Bare `ret` at 0x6F72F1. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled headless (DecompileAt, a copy of the project) and the element names checked against image strings: every name the function pushes is one of the seven, each `call [vt+0x48]` or `[vt+0x4C]` on the window result stored to the offsets above, each registration `call [[elem+0x48]+4]` with the observer address. Caller list: findRefs --callers 0x6F6E00 gives only 0x6F6831. Shown wrong by a second binding of any of these offsets elsewhere in the constructor (0x6F5C00-0x6F685B was read for its element names and has none).

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen_ShowDisplayMode
addresses.comment: **Writes resolution_value and refreshrate_value.** The resolution is the chosen display mode's (+0x110) width, `x`, height - `1920x1080` - built with itoa and no localisation; where g_SettingsPendingDisplayMode is not -1 (an OnApply has chosen a mode that needs a restart) it is the chosen one followed by the pending one in brackets, `1920x1080 (1600x900)`. The refresh rate is the chosen mode's rate at +0x114 and ` Hz` - `60 Hz` - or, where g_SettingsPendingRefreshRate is not -1, `60 Hz (75 Hz)` with the pending mode's pending rate. Both texts go into the instant text box's +0xD0. Called by the four resolution and refresh buttons' handlers and by CSettingsScreen_Refresh (0x6F9E56). `ret 4` at 0x6F9365. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled headless; the string literals `x` (VA 0x15D4A6C), ` Hz`, ` Hz (` and ` Hz)` are referenced from inside it (0x6F8710, 0x6F8EFA, 0x6F9121, 0x6F90C4), the tests are `cmp [0x170AEB0], -1` (0x6F864C) and `cmp [0x170AEB4], -1` (0x6F8E82). The `ret 4` and the five callers (findRefs --callers) each `push esi` before the call. Shown wrong by a localisation key or format string referenced from 0x6F8620-0x6F9365, of which the range's string scan found none.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::OnDecreaseMultisample

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::OnGammaSlider

It stores nothing - the settings' gamma is written only by StoreChoices - and neither Back nor closing undoes it (CIngameSettingsScreen::Close puts back the volumes and not the gamma); the saved gamma returns when the window is next opened, because CSettingsScreen_Refresh tells this observer. addresses.name: CGraphics_SetGamma
addresses.no_signature: The gamma arrives in XMM0 as a float (every caller does `cvtpd2ps xmm0, xmm0` just before the call) and the CGraphics on the stack, `ret 4`; a float in XMM0 is not a storage the record's signatures place.
addresses.comment: **The game's gamma: a straight ramp, scaled.** g = the float in XMM0 clamped to 0.1 .. 1.9; each of the 256 entries of all three channels = i * trunc(g * 65535) / 255, held to 0 .. 0xFFFF; then IDirect3DDevice9::SetGammaRamp(0, D3DSGR_CALIBRATE, ramp) on the device at CGraphics +0x64 (its slot 21). So the settings' `gamma` 50 is the identity, 0..5 are all 0.1, 95..100 all 1.9, and it is a brightness scale rather than a power curve. Callers: OnGammaSlider (0x6FABC3), StoreChoices (0x6F8285) and CGraphics' device setup (0xA6EFD4), each passing the settings' 0..100 value / 50. D3D9 applies a gamma ramp only in full screen (Direct3D's documentation, not this image). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xA76810-0xA768FD read whole: `comisd [0x160A3C0]` (0.1) and `[0x160A3B8]` (1.9) with the floats 0x15C05F8 = 0.1 and 0x160A3B0 = 1.9 as the clamps, `mulsd [0x160A3A8]` (65535.0), the `0x80808081` divide by 255 into three arrays at esp+8, +0x208, +0x408, and `push edx; push 1; push 0; push eax; call [ecx+0x54]` on [graphics+0x64]. Three callers from findRefs --callers, each `divsd [0x160A4C8]` (50.0) first. Shown wrong if +0x64 is not the device: slot 21 of IDirect3DDevice9 is SetGammaRamp by the SDK's vtable order.

addresses.name: GraphicsSettings_LoadKey

addresses.comment: **The `graphics = { ... }` block of settings.txt**, the graphics settings object embedded at GameSettings +8 (vftable 0x1600624, no RTTI; slot 4). Offsets are the object's own, GameSettings' in brackets: `adapter` +0x34 [+0x3C] (sscanf); `size` +0x38/+0x3C [+0x40/+0x44] (x, y), **a width under 1024 made 1024 and a height under 768 made 768**; `fullScreen` +0x44 [+0x4C]; `refreshRate` +0x40 [+0x48]; `shadows` +0x50 [+0x58]; `gamma` +0x54 [+0x5C], a float; `vsync` +0x32 [+0x3A]; `debugmonitor` +0x33 [+0x3B]; `shadowSize` +0x58 [+0x60], under 1 made 256, over 4096 made 4096, then through 0xAF9580; `anisotropic_filtering` +0x48 [+0x50]; `multi_sampling` +0x4C [+0x54]. addresses.name: GraphicsSettings_AddDisplayMode
addresses.signature: void __fastcall GraphicsSettings_AddDisplayMode(void* graphicsSettings@ECX, int height@ESI, int width@stack:4, int refreshRate@stack:8)
addresses.comment: Adds one enumerated mode to the display mode list (the object's +0xC .. +0x10, GameSettings +0x14 .. +0x18): where a DisplayMode of that width and height is already there, the refresh rate is appended to its rates (0x4221F0); otherwise a new DisplayMode {width, height, [refreshRate]} is appended (0xAA7A90). **No sorting and no duplicate test**: modes and rates stay in the order the driver enumerated them. Two exits, `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.

That 0x4221F0 appends and 0xAA7A90 appends rather than inserts sorted is inferred from their arguments - neither was read.

addresses.name: GraphicsSettings_EnumerateDisplayModes
addresses.comment: **Where the settings window's resolutions and refresh rates come from.** IDirect3D9::GetAdapterModeCount(**adapter 0**, D3DFMT_X8R8G8B8) and EnumAdapterModes for each, and every mode **at least 1024 wide and 720 high** goes through GraphicsSettings_AddDisplayMode with its width, height and refresh rate, logged `Usable res: `. The adapter is 0 whatever settings.txt's `adapter` says, and only the 32-bit format is asked. Called once, from CGraphics::CGraphics (0xA6E05A) with CGraphics +0x60. `ret 8` at 0xAA700B. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xAA6E33-0xAA6E7D: `call [ecx+0x18]` with `push 0x16; push 0 (ebx); push esi`, then in the loop `call [ecx+0x1C]` with `push eax (&mode); push edi; push 0x16; push ebx; push esi`, `cmp [esp+0x10], 0x400; jb` and `cmp [esp+0x14], 0x2D0; jb`; the AddDisplayMode call at 0xAA6FDC with ECX = [ebp+8], ESI = the height, width and refresh pushed. Vtable slots 6 and 7 of IDirect3D9 are GetAdapterModeCount and EnumAdapterModes by the SDK's order. findRefs --callers: 0xA6E05A only, `push [ebx+0x60]; push [ebp+0x10]`.

Where the display mode list has that exact size: with `lowestRefresh` the settings' refresh rate (+0x40) becomes the mode's lowest rate under 1000, 60 where it has none; without it GraphicsSettings_SnapRefreshRate; the size is kept. Where it has not and the settings are windowed (+0x44 clear), the size is kept as it is. Where it has not in full screen: modes of the same height and then of the same width are looked at (0xAA7A90 on each - read only this far), the line `The resolution "WxH" (or something similar) isn't supported by your screen. Please change resolution in settings.txt.` is logged and 1024x768 is answered. Two `ret 0x10`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.

addresses.name: GraphicsSettings_SnapRefreshRate
addresses.comment: Where the settings' refresh rate (+0x40, GameSettings +0x48) is not 0, replaces it with **the rate of `mode` nearest to it**, the first of equals. So the refresh rate the device is made with is always one the mode offers. `ret 8` at 0xAA79D5. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xAA7960-0xAA79D5 read whole: `test edx, edx` on [eax+0x40], the walk over the mode's +8..+0xC with `sub; cdq; xor; sub` (absolute difference) against a best starting at 100000, `jge` keeping the first of equals, and `mov [ecx+0x40], eax`. If the vector is empty the index stays -1 and the read is out of bounds - an empty mode cannot reach here from ValidateResolution's found path.

addresses.name: GraphicsSettings_DetectDevice
addresses.no_signature: The receiver arrives in ECX (its first store is [ecx+8] = 0x53E); whether it takes stack arguments was not established - the function was not read to its end. It is slot 6 of the graphics settings object's table (VA 0x1600624, no RTTI), called through it.
addresses.comment: graphicssettings.cpp's adapter and device check (`Graphic Adapters: `, `Using Adapter [`, multi-sampling), slot 6 of the graphics settings object (GameSettings +8, vftable VA 0x1600624, no RTTI). **Creates a test device with D3DCREATE_HARDWARE_VERTEXPROCESSING (0x40)** (0xAA47B8) and, failing that, **D3DCREATE_SOFTWARE_VERTEXPROCESSING (0x20)** (0xAA49D0), and writes whichever worked into the settings' behaviour flags (+0x1C, at 0xAA48BD and 0xAA4AD5) - never `D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE` (0x2). Calls Direct3DCreate9 at 0xAA3EEC (VAs). An `adapter` not below the adapter count is set to 0 with `Error in settings.txt. "adapter" has an invalid value. Setting it to 0.` **It fills g_MultisampleLevels**: for each of the 15 sample counts 2 to 16, IDirect3D9::CheckDeviceMultiSampleType(adapter, HAL, D3DFMT_X8R8G8B8, windowed = not fullScreen, samples, &quality); where it succeeds the entry's `supported` is set and its `max_quality` is the quality count less one, and the highest such count is kept; where it fails for the count settings.txt asked for (the object's +0x4C, which is GameSettings +0x54 `multi_sampling`, the object standing at GameSettings +8), that is logged `... samples NOT supported, yet set as option. Changing to 2 samples.` and +0x4C made 2. After the loop +0x4C is held to the highest supported count. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-luahost.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: The multisampling loop read off the listing 0xAA4392-0xAA4678: `mov edi, 2; mov [esp+0x54], 0x170A104; mov [esp+0xA4], 0xF` (15 turns), `call [edx+0x2C]` with `push &quality; push [entry-4]; push (byte [esi+0x44] == 0); push 0x16; push 1; push adapter; push d3d`, on success `dec ecx; mov [eax+4], ecx; mov byte [eax], 1; mov [esp+0x14], edi` (the highest, with two pushes on the stack), on failure `cmp [esi+0x4C], edi; jne` and the log line at VA 0x1600040 then `mov [edx+0x4C], 2` (0xAA464D), after the loop `cmp [ecx+0x4C], eax; jle; mov [ecx+0x4C], eax` (0xAA466B-0xAA4678). The slot: VA 0x160063C holds 0xAA3DD0, six after 0x1600624. What it adds is the table and the slot; the earlier comment's content is kept whole. Still inferred as a whole because it was not read to its end.

addresses.name: g_MultisampleLevels
addresses.comment: The 15 multisampling levels the game knows, sample counts 2 to 16 in order, each with whether the adapter supports it and its quality count, filled by GraphicsSettings_DetectDevice at startup. Device creation reads it for the settings' multisampling, and the settings window's two multisampling buttons step only through the supported ones; where none is, the window disables both (CSettingsScreen_Refresh). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: The static bytes from VA 0x170A100: {2,0,0}, {3,0,0} .. {16,0,0} at 12-byte steps; readers found by image.findValue: 0x6FA706, 0x6FA752, 0x6FA8C6, 0x6FA90D (the level) and 0x6F745D, 0x6F955B, 0x6F95DA, 0x6FA73E, 0x6FA901, 0xA6E1DA, 0xA6E20C (the flag), the writer 0xAA439B. The end bound 0x170A1B4 at 0x6FA718 and 0x6FA8D8; 0x170A1B8 is past it and belongs to something else (0xAA2C00..).

addresses.name: g_SettingsPendingDisplayMode
addresses.comment: The display mode an Apply chose that waits for a restart, as an index into the settings' display mode list, or -1: written only by OnApply (0x6F7497 / 0x6F74A4), -1 where the chosen mode and refresh rate are the ones running, the chosen index otherwise. Starts -1 and lasts the process. CSettingsScreen_ShowDisplayMode shows it in brackets after the chosen resolution. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Static value 0xFFFFFFFF. Every store found by a byte search over .text for `A3 B0 AE 70 01`, `89 0D ..` and `C7 05 ..`: 0x6F7497 and 0x6F74A4 only; readers 0x6F864C, 0x6F894B, 0x6F89D0, 0x6F90F3. The three hits in 0x7E0xxx-0x7E1xxx are `cmp reg, 0x170AEB0` end-of-array bounds of another table, not uses.

addresses.name: g_SettingsPendingRefreshRate
addresses.comment: The refresh rate an Apply chose that waits for a restart, as an index into the pending display mode's rates, or -1; set beside g_SettingsPendingDisplayMode by OnApply (0x6F74B4), -1 when nothing waits. CSettingsScreen_ShowDisplayMode shows it in brackets after the chosen rate. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Static value 0xFFFFFFFF; the one store `mov [0x170AEB4], eax` at 0x6F74B4, eax being -1 on the no-change path (0x6F7494 `or eax, -1`) and +0x114 otherwise; the read `cmp [0x170AEB4], -1` in ShowDisplayMode. The 0x7E0CD4 hit is a `cmp eax, 0x170AEB4` bound.

addresses.name: g_CounterScale
addresses.comment: counter_scale as the counters draw with it - every counter's scale is multiplied through it (CCounterObject::Render, _DrawShield, _DrawTexts, HitTest, _DrawBatch read it). Written by CSettings' constructor (1.0), by CMapRenderingOptions::LoadKey for `counter_scale`, and by CSettingsScreen::StoreChoices - so a change in the settings window shows on the next frame. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 3, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: findValue(0x170AF84): writers 0x45F6EE (LoadKey, `movss [0x170AF84], xmm0`), 0x45FB2E (the constructor), 0x6F817C (StoreChoices); readers 0x838EFB, 0x838F94, 0x839171, 0x839650, 0x839847, each in a recorded CCounterObject function by functionStart. The record already names it in GameSettings +0x100's comment and nowhere as an address.

struct_fields.name: width

struct_fields.name: height

struct_fields.name: refresh_rates
struct_fields.comment: The first of the size's refresh rates, in Hz, in enumeration order: an int vector's begin.
struct_fields.evidence: AddDisplayMode's new element has its vector at [ebp-0x20] beside width [ebp-0x28] and height [ebp-0x24]; the refresh handlers count `(+0xC - +8) >> 2`; ShowDisplayMode reads `[[mode+8] + index*4]`.

struct_fields.name: refresh_rates_end
struct_fields.comment: The end of the refresh rates.
struct_fields.evidence: As refresh_rates: the count is (+0xC - +8) / 4 in OnDecreaseRefreshRate and SnapRefreshRate (0xAA7976).

struct_fields.name: samples
struct_fields.comment: The sample count, 2 to 16.
struct_fields.evidence: Static {2..16} at VA 0x170A100 by 12; the window's handlers store it as the chosen level.

struct_fields.name: supported
struct_fields.comment: Set by GraphicsSettings_DetectDevice where CheckDeviceMultiSampleType succeeded.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov byte [eax], 1` with eax at 0x170A104 + 12n (0xAA4409); tested `cmp byte [..*4+0x170A104], 0` by both handlers.

struct_fields.name: max_quality
struct_fields.comment: CheckDeviceMultiSampleType's quality count less one.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov ecx, [esp+0xAC]; dec ecx; mov [eax+4], ecx` (0xAA43EB-0xAA43F9), eax at the flag.

struct_fields.name: display_modes
struct_fields.comment: The first of the screen sizes the adapter offers (the embedded graphics settings' +0xC), filled at startup by GraphicsSettings_EnumerateDisplayModes; the settings window steps through it. Not saved.
struct_fields.evidence: The window reads `[settings+0x14]` as the list's begin and `[settings+0x18]` as its end in every handler (0x6FA5B0, 0x6F734F); AddDisplayMode works on `[ecx+0xC]` of the object at +8.

struct_fields.name: display_modes_end
struct_fields.comment: The end of display_modes.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov ecx, [eax+0x18]; sub ecx, [eax+0x14]` then the divide by 24 (0x6F93C4).

struct_fields.name: size_x
struct_fields.comment: settings.txt `graphics = { size = { x } }`: the width the device is made at the next start. The settings window's CSettingsScreen::OnApply writes the chosen mode's width here; the running screen is CGraphics +0x6B9BC.
struct_fields.evidence: GraphicsSettings_LoadKey's `size` case reads into the object's +0x38 (GameSettings +0x40); OnApply stores the chosen DisplayMode's +0 here (0x6F7532).

struct_fields.name: size_y
struct_fields.comment: settings.txt `size = { y }`: the height, as size_x.
struct_fields.evidence: The `size` case's second int (+0x3C of the object); OnApply stores the chosen DisplayMode's +4 here (0x6F752F).

struct_fields.name: refresh_rate
struct_fields.comment: settings.txt `refreshRate`, in Hz; snapped to the nearest the mode offers at device creation (GraphicsSettings_SnapRefreshRate). CSettingsScreen::OnApply writes the chosen rate.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's token 0x5F (refreshRate) writes the object's +0x40; the window's search compares rates with `[settings+0x48]` (0x6F7431, 0x6F9471) and OnApply stores here (0x6F75AC).

struct_fields.name: multi_sampling
struct_fields.comment: settings.txt `multi_sampling`: the sample count, 0 for none; held at startup to what the adapter supports. CSettingsScreen::OnApply writes the chosen level where it differs, which asks for a restart.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's token 0x184 writes the object's +0x4C; the window reads `[esi+0x54]` (0x6F9547) and Apply writes `mov [edx+0x54], ecx` (0x6F7471).

struct_fields.name: gamma
struct_fields.comment: settings.txt `gamma`, 0 to 100, 50 the identity: CGraphics_SetGamma is given gamma / 50. Default 50.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's token 0x75 reads a float into the object's +0x54; StoreChoices stores the slider's value here (0x6F826A) and CSettingsScreen_Refresh reads it (0x6F992C); GraphicsSettings_Construct writes 50.0.

struct_fields.name: render_trees
struct_fields.comment: The `renderTrees` key of the map rendering options (+0xDC): trees_checkbox. StoreChoices also sets or clears bit 0 of the layer mask +0xEC with it, which the map objects' visibility reads each frame. Default yes.
struct_fields.evidence: CMapRenderingOptions::LoadKey's token 0x1CD (renderTrees, saveTokens.json) is `add ecx, 8` on the options at +0xDC (0x45F66D); StoreChoices 0x6F80C8-0x6F80EA; CSettings' constructor writes 0x10001 to +0xE4.

struct_fields.name: simple_water
struct_fields.comment: The `simpleWater` key: water_checkbox's opposite - ticked (`Advanced Water`) writes 0. Read where the water is drawn (0x85FB0F, through a settings pointer held at +0x42E4 of the drawing object). Default no.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's token 0x404 (simpleWater) is `add ecx, 9` (0x45F67D); StoreChoices `sete` into +0xE5 (0x6F80FE); a sweep of .text for byte accesses at +0xE5 found 10, of which these, the window's read and 0x85FB0F are the only settings ones (positive control: the sweep finds both known accesses).

struct_fields.name: waves
struct_fields.comment: The `waves` key; not on the settings window. Default yes.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's token 0x5C1 (waves) is `add ecx, 0xA` (0x45F698); read at 0x858859; CSettings' constructor's 0x10001 at +0xE4 leaves +0xE6 = 1.

struct_fields.name: unit_names_changed
struct_fields.comment: Set by CSettingsScreen::StoreChoices only where show_unit_names changed; the in-game frame (0x641D00, from 0x656F64) and a second reader (0x69EB00) see it, have 0x689E30 make every unit's counter name again (it calls CUnit_RefreshCounterName) and clear it.
struct_fields.evidence: The one write of 1 at 0x6F812E behind `cmp cl, [eax+0xe9]; je`; the readers `cmp byte [eax+0xEA], 0` then `call 0x689E30` then `mov byte [eax+0xEA], 0` at 0x641D08-0x641D21 and 0x69EB2F-0x69EB48 (found by a scan of every GetGameSettings call); 0x689E30's only call is 0x5BE500. That it loops over every unit is inferred.

struct_fields.name: d3d
struct_fields.comment: The IDirect3D9 the device is made from; GraphicsSettings_EnumerateDisplayModes asks its adapter modes.
struct_fields.evidence: CGraphics::CGraphics pushes [ebx+0x60] to EnumerateDisplayModes (0xA6E052), which calls its slots 6 and 7 (GetAdapterModeCount, EnumAdapterModes); the record's CGraphics_CreateDevice comment calls CreateDevice through the object at +0x60.

struct_fields.name: d3d_device
struct_fields.comment: The IDirect3DDevice9; CGraphics_SetGamma calls its slot 21, SetGammaRamp.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov eax, [ebp+8]; mov eax, [eax+0x64]; ... call [ecx+0x54]` with (0, 1, ramp) at 0xA768E1-0xA768F6. Likely the device: slot 21 with those arguments is SetGammaRamp by the SDK's order; nothing else was checked.

struct_fields.name: graphics_settings
struct_fields.comment: The graphics settings object (GameSettings +8) the device was made from: GraphicsSettings_ValidateResolution is handed it and the device setup reads its gamma at +0x54.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov ecx, [ebx+0x6BC48]; ... push ecx; call 0xAA7010` (0xA6E05F-0xA6E072) and `mov ecx, [ebx+0x6BC48]; movss xmm0, [ecx+0x54]` before CGraphics_SetGamma (0xA6EFB9). That it points at GameSettings +8 rather than a copy is inferred.

struct_fields.name: chosen_display_mode
struct_fields.comment: The Video tab's resolution: an index into GameSettings' display_modes. Set to the running screen's on every opening; written to size_x/size_y by CSettingsScreen::OnApply. CSettingsScreen_Refresh sets it on every opening to the index of the mode whose size is the running screen's (CGraphics +0x6B9BC/+0x6B9C0), 0 where none is - so a windowed screen of a size the adapter does not list shows the first mode.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored by CSettingsScreen_Refresh (0x6F93B8, 0x6F9403), stepped by the two resolution handlers, read by ShowDisplayMode and OnApply (0x6F7401).

struct_fields.name: chosen_refresh_rate
struct_fields.comment: An index into the chosen display mode's refresh_rates; 0 after any change of resolution. CSettingsScreen_Refresh sets it on every opening to the index of settings +0x48 **in the first display mode's rates**, bounded by the chosen mode's count (the walk starts at list[0] +8, 0x6F949E) - a slip, so where the two modes' rates differ the index shown is not the saved rate's; 0 where it is not found. OnApply makes the same search for the running rate.
struct_fields.evidence: Zeroed by both resolution handlers, stepped by the refresh handlers, set by CSettingsScreen_Refresh (0x6F94D5), read by ShowDisplayMode and OnApply (0x6F754A). The slip: CSettingsScreen_Refresh 0x6F949E `mov eax, [edx+8]` with edx the list's first element, the bound reloaded from the chosen element at 0x6F94BF; OnApply's 0x6F7425-0x6F7428 the same.

struct_fields.name: chosen_multisampling
struct_fields.comment: The chosen sample count, 0 for none. CSettingsScreen_Refresh sets it from settings +0x54 where that is 2 or more and g_MultisampleLevels marks it supported (no bound above 16), else 0, and **disables both multisampling buttons where no level is supported** (slot 47, 0x6F97BF and 0x6F9875).
struct_fields.evidence: Set by CSettingsScreen_Refresh (0x6F9565), stepped by the multisample handlers, compared and written to GameSettings +0x54 by OnApply (0x6F7467). The greying: `call [edx+0xBC]` on the buttons found by the names decrease_/increase_multisample_button (0x6F9753, 0x6F9809) behind the any-supported loop over 0x170A104..0x170A1B8.

struct_fields.name: counter_distance_choice
struct_fields.comment: counter_slider's value, 0 to 100: the counter distance divided by five. StoreChoices writes value / 100 * 500 to counter_distance. CSettingsScreen_Refresh first writes the raw counter_distance here and then sets the slider and tells its observers, which puts the 0..100 value back; **a settings.gui without counter_slider leaves the raw distance, which StoreChoices then multiplies by five on every Apply.**
struct_fields.evidence: OnCounterSlider's store; CSettingsScreen_Refresh writes the raw distance first (0x6F9A1A); StoreChoices' conversion before +0xFC.

slots_noted: No function here is held by an RTTI vftable (vtable.py --holding for each: none). GraphicsSettings_LoadKey and GraphicsSettings_DetectDevice are slots 4 and 6 of the no-RTTI table at VA 0x1600624 (rva 0x1200624), which the record does not hold; its other slots are 0xAA3D70 (the destructor), 0x45BB10, 0xAA6AB0 (the graphics block's writer, reader C's), 0xA7C050, 0xABF890. The button, checkbox and scrollbar handlers are member pointers stored in CButtonObserverGlue / CCheckBoxObserverGlue / CScrollbarObserverGlue<CSettingsScreen> (VAs 0x15D4B0C, 0x15D4B38, 0x15D4B58), not virtuals.
